newsitem.title: INDIA: India revises divestment rules for unlisted shares.
newsitem.headline: India revises divestment rules for unlisted shares.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Wednesday it revised the valuation rules for divestment of unlisted or thinly traded shares by foreign investors.
RBI said it would automatically clear divestment transactions by non-residents in favour of residents upto a total value of two million rupees per company in a year at a mutually agreed price.
For transactions of more than two million rupees for thinly traded shares, RBI said the non-resident seller will have three options.
+ To sell the shares at higher of the price based on earnings per share linked to price earnings multiple and the price based on net asset value linked to its book value multiple.
+ To sell the shares on screen-based stock exchanges at the prevailing market price in small lots in not less than five trading days.
+ To sell the shares at a price based on independent valuations.
For transactions of more than two million rupees in shares of unlisted firms, RBI said the same rules would apply.
